header:
Date: 2026-01-08 15:00 UTC
Duration: 50 mins
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Voyager - Head of Platform), Rahul Menon (Voyager - SRE), Dianne Cho (Voyager - FinOps)
Recording: Enabled
Shared materials: https://redwood.ai/demos/route-mapping-deck.pdf, spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/pilots/voyager-cost-model.xlsx
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Voyager Systems through the Console route-mapping views, per-route cost breakdowns, and pilot options. Conversation focused on how tags and route grouping map to chargeback, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and security controls for private deployments. Next steps: security docs and pricing worksheet from Redwood; Voyager to share sample traffic and tagging; Redwood to provision a 1-week dedicated pilot for route-level telemetry and cost validation.
topics: Console tour: route map and per-route dashboards
Route tagging and grouping best practices
Dedicated pilot vs hosted API tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account. Marcus is our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:05] Lena Ortiz: Hey thanks, we are good. Quick heads up, Dianne will be tuned in for cost questions and Rahul's here for the SRE concerns.
[00:12] Marcus Patel: Hi all, Marcus here. Today we'll focus on the console route-mapping view and a per-route cost break down, show some filters, and then talk pilot options.
[00:20] Dianne Cho: Great, we really want to understand where costs are coming from at the route level, like per endpoint, not just a big bucket.
[00:28] Avery Chen: Totally. Quick agenda: 1) show route map and dashboards 2) cost decomposition + sample chargeback 3) pilot options 4) security/compliance notes. Any additions?
[00:36] Rahul Menon: Maybe show how tags from our side map into routes? We have a weird naming pattern in prod that might be a pain.
[00:42] Marcus Patel: Yeah we can demo mapping rules, and show live rename/aliasing.
[00:47] Marcus Patel: (screen share) Alright, console front page, this is the usage overview. You can see token volume trend, cost trend, and top routes by spend.
[01:05] Marcus Patel: Click into the route-map — this visualizes routes as a topology, edges are call volume and nodes are endpoints. You can hover on a node and get latency, p95, token cost, and calls/min.
[01:20] Lena Ortiz: That topology view is new, right? I hadn't seen it before.
[01:25] Avery Chen: We shipped that in the last console update — it helps platform teams identify hot paths.
[01:30] Marcus Patel: Now filter by tag. Here's 'customer:alpha' — you can see the route set narrows to the exact microservices that hit the inference API. This matches tag sync from our SDK or your proxy.
[01:45] Rahul Menon: For us the issue is that our routes come in as long URIs with query strings, can Redwood do normalization?
[01:52] Marcus Patel: Absolutely, we have normalization rules. You can strip query params, apply regex, or create alias rules. We'll map once you share the pattern.
[02:05] Dianne Cho: Show the cost breakdown for one route — like how do you attribute cost between model compute, batching overhead, and token spend?
[02:12] Marcus Patel: Good question. On the route detail page we show a stacked decomposition: model runtime cost (GPU hours amortized), queued/batching overhead, prefix cache hits, and token-based runtime cost. You can toggle quantization profiles and see pro forma cost if you switch to a smaller model.
[02:34] Marcus Patel: (clicks) Here, route "/nlp/summarize" — top shows p50/p95 latencies; below is spend: 62% model runtime, 20% batching overhead, 18% token delta.
[02:46] Lena Ortiz: That 20% batching overhead, that's the extra tail time from small bursts, correct?
[02:50] Marcus Patel: Yeah. We surface a batching inefficiency score. If your request pattern is a lot of tiny, async calls, that increases per-token cost.
[02:58] Rahul Menon: Could we get a view that flags routes over a cost-per-1000-token threshold? We want alerts for runaway endpoints.
[03:04] Marcus Patel: You can create a route-alert rule — threshold on cost per token, or cost delta week-over-week. It integrates with Slack or PagerDuty.
[03:12] Dianne Cho: And billing export — can we map routes to internal chargeback codes? Our finance team needs that.
[03:18] Avery Chen: Yes, the export includes a route->tag column and a recommended mapping UI where finance can assign charge codes. We can also push to your billing system via webhooks.
[03:28] Lena Ortiz: How does Redwood handle private deployments? If we do a VPC/private controller, does the console still show route costing?
[03:35] Marcus Patel: The console can be run in a hybrid model. For private deployments we ship a local collector that aggregates telemetry to your private control plane; cost attribution runs locally and the console in Redwood's region displays the aggregated metrics, or you can host the console behind your VPC.
[03:54] Rahul Menon: Any KMS or HSM support? We can't have keys in a shared service.
[03:59] Marcus Patel: We integrate with customer KMS for model encryption keys and audit logs. For fully air-gapped setups we have an on-prem package.
[04:08] Dianne Cho: SOC2 scope? We need to give the compliance team something quick.
[04:12] Avery Chen: We'll send the SOC2 report and a compliance brief. I'll include an architecture note for where logs and audit trails are stored.
[04:20] Marcus Patel: Back to the dashboard — here's a view comparing two models across the same route. You can overlay latency and cost per token. Very useful for deciding quantization or model switch rollouts.
[04:35] Lena Ortiz: Ooh, can you do canary rollouts per route? Like 10% traffic to cheaper model?
[04:39] Marcus Patel: Yes, rollouts can be route-scoped. You can set percent traffic, duration, and automatic rollback rules tied to quality regressions or latency SLO breaches.
[04:48] Rahul Menon: What metrics do you look at for quality regressions? We can't have hallucination checks at scale.
[04:55] Marcus Patel: We integrate post-processing evals — can run a set of prompt-based unit tests, embedding drift checks, and token delta on reranks. For hallucinations you'd wire up a small eval set or monitor conversational drift with user-feedback events.
[05:12] Dianne Cho: For the cost model, do you show cost-per-route per day and roll that up to week/month for chargebacks?
[05:18] Marcus Patel: Yep, time granularity is configurable. We also produce a predictive run rate if you keep current traffic and apply seasonal smoothing.
[05:27] Lena Ortiz: On the UI, can you annotate routes with owner and SLA? We want the platform team responsibilities in the same view.
[05:33] Marcus Patel: You can add metadata to a route: owner, SLA, project code. That metadata is included in exports and appears on hover cards.
[05:40] Avery Chen: Quick pause — does that align with what you need for chargeback?
[05:44] Dianne Cho: Mostly, yes. The only gap is we need to include non-inference costs — like preprocessing services and database calls — in a consolidated dashboard. Can Redwood ingest external cost signals?
[05:56] Marcus Patel: We can ingest tags from your cloud billing exports and correlate by route tags. It's not perfect but it lets you do blended chargeback. We'll show an example in the pilot.
[06:06] Rahul Menon: About pilot — what does a dedicated pilot include? We want realistic numbers.
[06:10] Marcus Patel: For this pilot we propose a 7-day dedicated pool with a small reserved GPU set, route telemetry turned on, and a benchmark harness to replay your 72h traffic sample. We'll run i) cost breakdown, ii) latency distribution, iii) batching efficiency, iv) cache hit impact.
[06:24] Avery Chen: We'll instrument with a lightweight tracer to map incoming requests to routes. Marcus will provide the test plan.
[06:30] Lena Ortiz: What's the expected lead time to spin up the pilot? We can provide credentials tomorrow.
[06:35] Marcus Patel: If we get the traffic sample and route mappings we can provision in 3 business days.
[06:40] Dianne Cho: Budget question — what's the pricing model for a week-long dedicated pilot?
[06:45] Avery Chen: Usually pilots are discounted; Marcus will include an estimated cost sheet — the pricing worksheet I send will have the baseline for reserved pool + token estimates.
[06:53] Marcus Patel: I'm dropping a quick demo link in the chat — sample cost model for a 7-day run: https://redwood.app/pilots/example-costs.csv
[07:00] Lena Ortiz: (reads) Nice. For normal ops we will almost certainly want route-level alerts and tagging automation. Do you have automation for tag injection from our API gateway?
[07:09] Marcus Patel: Yes, we have integrations for common gateways and SDKs. For custom gateways we provide a small middleware snippet to attach route metadata.
[07:17] Rahul Menon: What about edge inference? We have some latency-sensitive endpoints that might need local runtime.
[07:22] Marcus Patel: Edge is possible with our on-prem runtime. For those endpoints you can run local inference and only send aggregated telemetry back; cost calculation in the console supports hybrid (remote + edge) mapping.
[07:33] Dianne Cho: A few of our questions from procurement: contract length, SLA, data residency.
[07:38] Avery Chen: We have usage-based month-to-month for hosted, 12/36-month reserved for dedicated with SLA tiers. Data residency options via region pinning or private deployment. I'll include a contract template.
[07:49] Marcus Patel: Another note — the console also has a "what-if" pane. You can flip to simulate moving a route to a smaller model and estimate cost delta and latency impact.
[07:58] Lena Ortiz: That will help our product folks decide where to optimize.
[08:02] Rahul Menon: For the sample normalization rules, what format do you need? Regex examples?
[08:08] Marcus Patel: Regex or a small CSV of example input->normalized route pairs. That works fine.
[08:13] Dianne Cho: If we do the pilot, will Redwood share raw telemetry or only aggregated metrics? Finance needs the raw exports.
[08:18] Marcus Patel: We can provide raw exports (anonymized on request) and the aggregated dashboards. For private deployments raw telemetry stays in your environment.
[08:29] Avery Chen: Okay, let's do a short demo of the mass export and the chargeback mapping UI.
[08:33] Marcus Patel: (screen) Export UI: choose date range, include route tags, include owner metadata. Here's a sample CSV — route, tokens, compute_ms, batch_overhead_ms, cost_usd.
[08:45] Lena Ortiz: Looks straightforward. We will test mapping to our GL codes.
[08:50] Rahul Menon: One more thing — how do you handle cold start for models with large KV caches? We saw warmup costs in another vendor.
[08:58] Marcus Patel: We surface cache warmup as part of the cost analysis. Our KV cache persistence and pre-warming policies reduce that; you can pin a model warm pool during business hours. We'll show the numbers in the pilot.
[09:12] Dianne Cho: Final question from my side: export retention. How long do you keep raw telemetry?
[09:18] Avery Chen: Default is 90 days for raw telemetry in hosted; longer retention is available as an add-on or for dedicated customers. Private installs are under your control.
[09:29] Lena Ortiz: That answers most of our concerns. Let's recap next steps.
[09:33] Avery Chen: Recap: We'll send SOC2 and pricing worksheet, Marcus will provision pilot test plan, Voyager will share tagging rules and 72h traffic dump. Action items in the chat.
[09:42] Rahul Menon: Sounds good. When should we reconvene after the pilot?
[09:46] Marcus Patel: We suggest a post-pilot review within 3 business days of pilot end, to go over real numbers and recommend optimizations.
[09:54] Dianne Cho: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[09:57] Avery Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with the attachments and next steps.
[10:00] (call ends)
